description: A Chrome-only SPA + local Node.js scan pipeline that discovers developer talent by analysing public GitHub repositories — replacing self-reported CVs with verifiable, commit-level evidence. Surfaces ranked candidates via structured faceted search with independent Skill Score and AI Maturity Score dimensions.

userStories.title: Project initialization and monorepo scaffold
userStories.description: Scaffold the monorepo from the starter kit at setup/tools/claude-code-mastery-project-starter-kit into eggs/candidate-skill-scanner/. Install all dependencies (React 18, Vite 5, TypeScript 5.4+, Tailwind 3, shadcn/ui, Radix UI, Lucide React, React Router v6, TanStack Query v5, Zustand v4, React Hook Form, Zod, Classpresso, Firebase SDK, Octokit, simple-git, Commander.js, Vitest, Playwright). Generate CLAUDE.md following starter kit format. Initialize git and confirm pnpm install succeeds.
acceptanceCriteria: Directory candidate-skill-scanner/ exists with starter kit as base
package.json initialised with project name candidate-skill-scanner and all dependency groups listed
pnpm install runs successfully with no errors
CLAUDE.md exists and follows the starter kit format with project-specific instructions
git is initialized with an initial commit
pnpm dev starts without errors and loads a blank index.html at localhost:3000
userStories.notes: Use setup/tools/claude-code-mastery-project-starter-kit as the base. This is the foundation for all subsequent stories — do not proceed until pnpm install is clean.

userStories.title: TypeScript targets, Tailwind/Vite config, and Firebase emulator setup
userStories.description: Configure three tsconfig files extending a shared strict base (tsconfig.app.json for DOM/React, tsconfig.pipeline.json for Node.js, tsconfig.functions.json for Firebase Functions). Configure Vite targeting src/app/main.tsx on port 3000 with postbuild Classpresso hook. Configure Tailwind with Direction 2 tokens (slate-900 nav, slate-50 body, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono). Wire up Firebase project config, emulators (Firestore + Auth), .env.example, and .env.local for local development.
acceptanceCriteria: tsconfig.json (base, strict=true, @/* paths), tsconfig.app.json (DOM+ES2022), tsconfig.pipeline.json (Node+ES2022), tsconfig.functions.json all exist and pnpm typecheck passes with zero errors
vite.config.ts targets src/app/main.tsx, serves port 3000, uses @vitejs/plugin-react; pnpm build succeeds
tailwind.config.ts includes Direction 2 tokens: slate-900, slate-50, Space Grotesk as default sans, JetBrains Mono as mono; postbuild script invokes classpresso optimize
firebase.json exists with Hosting SPA rewrite and Functions config; .env.example documents all VITE_FIREBASE_* vars and GITHUB_PAT
firebase emulators:start launches Firestore + Auth emulators successfully
GitHub Actions CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml runs typecheck + test:unit + build on every push; deploy step gated on main branch
userStories.notes: Three tsconfigs must prevent DOM/Node cross-contamination. tsconfig.pipeline.json must NOT include DOM lib. The postbuild Classpresso hook is required by the starter kit.

userStories.title: Shared TypeScript types and centralized Firestore wrapper
userStories.description: Define all shared TypeScript types in src/types/ (Candidate with aiMaturityScore: number | null, Repository, AiConfigFileSignal, ScanJob with all payload variants, TaxonomyItem, AdminFlag, SearchQueryParams). Create a pipeline-specific scoring output type that explicitly excludes aiMaturityScore fields. Implement the centralized Firestore wrapper at src/core/db/firestore.ts with typed get/set/update/delete/query/collection/serverTimestamp methods, auto-detecting emulator from VITE_USE_EMULATOR env var.
acceptanceCriteria: src/types/candidate.ts exports Candidate with aiMaturityScore: number | null — never a numeric sentinel for unscored state
src/types/repository.ts exports Repository and AiConfigFileSignal; src/types/scan-job.ts exports ScanJob, ScanJobStatus, ScanJobType, DiscoverPayload, ScanRepoPayload, RescanPayload
src/types/taxonomy.ts exports TaxonomyItem and TaxonomyCategory; src/types/admin.ts exports AdminFlag, AdminFlagType, AdminFlagStatus, SearchQueryParams
A pipeline scoring output type exists that TypeScript-enforces the absence of aiMaturityScore, aiMaturityScoredAt, aiMaturityScoredBy — preventing pipeline writes from overwriting manual scores
src/core/db/firestore.ts exports typed wrapper methods, detects VITE_USE_EMULATOR and routes to emulator, importable from both src/app and src/pipeline
Unit test verifies the wrapper routes to emulator in test environment; pnpm typecheck passes with all types defined
userStories.notes: The null vs 0 distinction for aiMaturityScore is a hard invariant — null means not evaluated, 0 means evaluated as Level 0. This must be enforced at the type level throughout. All Firestore access must go through the wrapper — never direct SDK calls.

userStories.title: Firestore security rules, composite indexes, and seed taxonomy
userStories.description: Write and deploy Firestore security rules enforcing: unauthenticated = no access; authenticated non-admin = read candidates/repositories/taxonomy; authenticated admin = read/write all collections. Define all required composite indexes in firestore.indexes.json for candidates, repositories, scan_jobs, admin_flags, and taxonomy. Create and run an idempotent seed script that populates the taxonomy collection with curated seed items (Languages, Frameworks, Tools, AI Agent Patterns, AI Maturity Levels) from a version-controlled scripts/seeds/taxonomy.json.
acceptanceCriteria: firestore.rules enforces the three-tier access model (unauthenticated/authenticated/admin); integration test confirms non-admin token cannot read admin_flags

firestore.indexes.json defines all composite indexes from the architecture spec: candidates (skillTags+skillScore, skillTags+aiMaturityScore, skillTags+lastScanned, aiMaturityScore+skillScore, isStale+lastScanned), repositories (owner+lastScanned, scanStatus+lastPushedAt), scan_jobs (status+createdAt, status+priority+createdAt, status+failedAt), admin_flags (type+status+createdAt, type+status+resultCount), taxonomy (category+isSearchable+sortOrder, isSearchable+candidateCount)
scripts/seeds/taxonomy.json exists with seed items covering Languages (10+), Frameworks (10+), Tools (10+), AI Agent Patterns (6+), AI Maturity Levels (0-5)
Seed script is idempotent — running twice does not duplicate taxonomy items; each item has isSeeded: true, isSearchable: true, candidateCount: 0, correct sortOrder and displayName
pnpm db:query --seed taxonomy (or equivalent) runs the seed script against emulator successfully
Integration test (Vitest + emulator) verifies a valid candidate composite index query returns results correctly
userStories.notes: Seed taxonomy is critical — the Search UI (Epic 5) depends on it for facet panel rendering. The composite indexes must match the query patterns in src/handlers/search.ts exactly.

userStories.title: Google Sign-In, route guards, server-side admin verification, and admin CLI
userStories.description: Implement Google Sign-In via Firebase Auth with redirect to /search on success. Build PrivateRoute (all routes) and AdminRoute (/admin/*) React components reading admin status from Firebase ID token custom claim. Implement verify-admin-claim Firebase Function for server-side claim verification. Implement scripts/admin-ops.ts CLI command to grant admin role via Firebase Admin SDK custom claims.
acceptanceCriteria: Login page renders a Sign in with Google button; successful Google OAuth redirects to /search; user avatar and display name appear in top nav; sign-out returns to login
PrivateRoute redirects unauthenticated users to /login; AdminRoute redirects non-admin authenticated users to /search; both guards show loading state while auth resolves (no flash of redirect)
Admin status is read from Firebase ID token custom claim (admin: true) — NOT from Firestore or client-side state
verify-admin-claim Firebase Function rejects tokens without admin: true claim with 403; unit test verifies this

pnpm admin:ops grant-admin --uid <firebase-uid> sets custom claim { admin: true } on the specified user via Firebase Admin SDK; script follows starter kit registered CLI pattern in scripts/admin-ops.ts
Firebase Auth emulator is used in test environment; Vitest test confirms AdminRoute blocks non-admin token
userStories.notes: Admin role grant is CLI-only — no web UI path must exist for role elevation. The AdminRoute guard must enforce server-side claims, not client-side state. All auth tests run against the Firebase Auth emulator.

userStories.title: CLI entry point and Firestore-backed job queue
userStories.description: Implement the Commander.js CLI entry point at src/pipeline/index.ts with scan discover, scan rescan, and scan status sub-commands (all with correct options). Implement the Firestore-backed job queue: ScanJob document creation in scan_jobs, worker polling loop (every 10s), atomic status transitions (pending → running → completed/failed), exponential backoff retry (2^attempts minutes, max 3 attempts), rate-limit-aware pause via rateLimitedUntil field.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm scan --help shows discover, rescan, status sub-commands; each sub-command shows correct options with --help
pnpm scan discover --query 'test' --limit 10 creates a discover ScanJob in scan_jobs with status: pending, correct payload, priority: 0, attempts: 0, maxAttempts: 3
Worker polls for pending jobs ordered by priority DESC, createdAt ASC; picks up one job at a time; sets status to running with lastAttemptAt

On job success: status → completed with completedAt; on failure with attempts < maxAttempts: status → pending (retry); on failure with attempts >= maxAttempts: status → failed with errorMessage and failedAt
A rate-limited job sets rateLimitedUntil timestamp and remains pending until that time passes; worker skips it until then
Failed jobs do not crash the worker — subsequent jobs are processed; unit test verifies full job lifecycle: enqueue → pick up → complete
userStories.notes: The worker is single-threaded in MVP — one job at a time. The Firestore-backed queue (no Redis/BullMQ) is intentional at this scale. All pipeline code runs via tsx and targets tsconfig.pipeline.json.

userStories.title: GitHub API adapter, repo discovery, deduplication, and rate-limit pacing
userStories.description: Implement the GitHub API adapter at src/adapters/github.ts wrapping Octokit behind the source-agnostic interface at src/adapters/source-adapter.ts. Implement the discover job handler: query GitHub Search API, extract repo surface metadata, deduplicate against existing repositories collection, write new Repository docs with scanStatus: surface, enqueue scan-repo jobs with targetDepth: layer1. Enforce rate-limit-aware pacing: read X-RateLimit-Remaining/Reset headers, throttle when <100 remaining, set rateLimitedUntil on 429/403 responses.
acceptanceCriteria: src/adapters/source-adapter.ts defines the source-agnostic interface; src/adapters/github.ts implements it via Octokit — all GitHub API calls go through this adapter
pnpm scan discover --query 'python fastapi' --limit 50 queries GitHub Search API and returns repos with: fullName, primaryLanguage, starCount, forkCount, lastPushedAt, topics
Repos already in repositories collection (by fullName) are not re-enqueued; a second discover call with the same query returns 0 new repos if all were already stored
New Repository docs written with scanStatus: surface; a scan-repo job enqueued per new repo with targetDepth: layer1; CLI outputs summary of N discovered, M new enqueued
Adapter reads X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset from every response; throttles when remaining < 100; sets rateLimitedUntil on 429/403 responses
Integration test (mocked GitHub API) verifies 429 response causes job re-queue with correct rateLimitedUntil; unit test verifies deduplication logic
userStories.notes: GITHUB_PAT must be read from .env — never hardcoded. The source-adapter interface is required by NFR15 for future GitLab/Bitbucket support. Layer 1 cost is ~2 API calls per repo (metadata + languages endpoint).

userStories.title: Local repo cloning and Layer 1 analysis
userStories.description: Implement the scan-repo job handler for targetDepth: layer1. Clone repos using simple-git (shallow --depth 1 for Layer 1). Run Layer 1 analysis at src/pipeline/analysis/layer1.ts: detect primary language, parse package files (package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pom.xml) to extract frameworks/tools, normalise against taxonomy, flag unknown signals as isSearchable: false taxonomy items. Always delete clone directory after analysis (success or failure). Update Repository doc with layer1 fields and scanStatus: layer1.
acceptanceCriteria: scan-repo job with targetDepth: layer1 clones the repo to a temporary directory using simple-git --depth 1
Clone directory is always deleted after analysis completes, whether the analysis succeeds or fails
Layer 1 analysis detects primary language from file extensions and GitHub language metadata
package.json (Node/JS), requirements.txt/pyproject.toml (Python), Cargo.toml (Rust), go.mod (Go), pom.xml/build.gradle (Java) are parsed for framework and tool dependencies
Detected dependencies are normalised against taxonomy IDs; previously-unseen signals are stored as taxonomy items with isSearchable: false for later review

Repository.detectedFrameworks, detectedTools, detectedDependencies updated; scanStatus set to layer1; unit test verifies correct framework extraction from sample package.json and requirements.txt fixtures
userStories.notes: Layer 1 uses no additional GitHub API calls — all work is on the shallow clone. The system must support up to 50 concurrent ephemeral clones per NFR9 without exhausting local disk.

userStories.title: Layer 2 analysis — commit patterns, ownership, and test coverage
userStories.description: Implement Layer 2 analysis at src/pipeline/analysis/layer2.ts using a full-depth clone (simple-git without --depth flag, reading up to 200 commits). Extract: commit count, commit span in months, ownership detection (isOwnerRepo = true if repo owner is dominant committer with >50% of commits), test directory detection (tests/, __tests__/, spec/), test file count, estimated test coverage level (none/low/medium/high). Update Repository doc with layer2 fields and scanStatus: layer2.
acceptanceCriteria: scan-repo job with targetDepth: layer2 performs a full clone (not shallow) to access full commit history
Commit count and commit span in months computed via simple-git log
isOwnerRepo set to true if the repository owner is the dominant committer (>50% of commits by author email matching owner username)
Test coverage signals detected: presence of test directories (tests/, __tests__/, spec/), test file count; estimatedTestCoverage assigned: none (0 test files), low (<10), medium (10-50), high (50+)
Repository.commitCount, firstCommitAt, lastCommitAt, commitSpanMonths, isOwnerRepo, hasTestDirectory, estimatedTestCoverage written to Firestore; scanStatus set to layer2
Clone deleted after analysis; unit test verifies ownership detection logic with mock git log fixture
userStories.notes: Layer 2 requires a full clone — not shallow. Use git log --format='%H %ae %ad' -n 200 for commit history. The full clone is more expensive on disk — delete it promptly after analysis.

userStories.title: AI tooling signal detection and config file evolution tracking
userStories.description: Implement AI signal detection at src/pipeline/analysis/ai-signals.ts. Detect known AI config files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .cursor/rules, .cursor/settings.json, ai-context.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .aider*). For each detected config file: extract firstDetectedAt from git log, count modification commits (modificationCount), classify diffComplexity (minimal <10 lines, moderate <100, extensive >=100), set isEvolved = modificationCount > 3, set originSignal (likely-copied if introduced in single large commit matching known templates, else likely-original). Detect co-authored-by AI trailers and attribution patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: All listed AI config file patterns are detected in the cloned repo file tree
For each detected AI config file: firstDetectedAt set from first git commit touching that file, modificationCount = number of commits touching the file, lastModifiedAt = most recent such commit
diffComplexity classified: minimal (<10 total lines changed across all modifications), moderate (<100), extensive (>=100); isEvolved = modificationCount > 3
originSignal: likely-copied if file was introduced in a single commit with >50 lines (copy paste heuristic); likely-original otherwise; unknown if insufficient data
coAuthoredByAI: true if any commit trailer contains Co-authored-by: with a known AI tool name (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, etc.)
Repository.aiConfigFiles (AiConfigFileSignal[]), coAuthoredByAI, aiAttributionPatterns written to Firestore; unit test verifies AiConfigFileSignal population from mock git log with CLAUDE.md
userStories.notes: Use git log --follow --format='%H %ae %ad' -- <filename> to trace each config file's history. The AI signals are the raw data for manual AI Maturity Score assignment — accuracy matters more than completeness at this stage.

userStories.title: Skill Score computation and candidate profile generation
userStories.description: Implement Skill Score computation at src/pipeline/scoring/skill-score.ts using the deterministic formula from the architecture spec. Derive the candidate record from the repo's owner GitHub username. Create or update the Candidate document in Firestore with all pipeline-owned fields. The pipeline scoring output type must TypeScript-enforce the absence of aiMaturityScore fields. Set isStale as a denormalized boolean at write time (lastScanned > 90 days). Update taxonomy candidateCount via the Firebase Function post-scan trigger.
acceptanceCriteria: computeSkillScore implements the exact formula: primaryLanguage (20) + frameworks capped at 30 (6 each) + tools capped at 15 (5 each) + commitSpan capped at 10 + ownership bonus (10) + test coverage (0/3/8/15) + AI signals capped at 10; clamped 0-100
aiMaturityScore is NOT set or modified by the pipeline — the scoring output type excludes aiMaturityScore, aiMaturityScoredAt, aiMaturityScoredBy at the TypeScript type level

Candidate document created or updated: skillScore, skillTags (flat merged taxonomy ID array), detectedLanguages, detectedFrameworks, detectedTools, aiToolingSignals, aiAgentPatterns, repoCount, primaryRepoIds, commitSpanMonths, lastScanned, isStale, scanDepth
isStale is computed at write time: true if Date.now() - lastScanned > 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; never computed at query time
Candidate is derived from the repo owner's GitHub username as the Firestore document ID
Unit test verifies computeSkillScore returns the correct score for a known input set; end-to-end: pnpm scan discover + worker processes jobs + candidate appears in Firestore
userStories.notes: The aiMaturityScore protection is the most critical invariant in the codebase — a pipeline rescan must never overwrite a manually assigned score. TypeScript type exclusion is the enforcement mechanism, not runtime checks.

userStories.title: App shell, routing, taxonomy facet panel, and URL state management
userStories.description: Build the React app shell with top nav (h-12, slate-900, Space Grotesk branding, user avatar, sign-out), React Router v6 routes (/login, /search, /candidates/:id, /admin/*), three-zone layout (top nav + left facet panel w-64 + main content). Implement the FacetPanel component with five collapsible category sections (Languages, Frameworks, Tools, AI Agent Usage Patterns, AI Maturity Level) using fieldset/legend for WCAG 2.1 AA. Implement useSearchQuery hook that owns URL-encoded facet state via useSearchParams.
acceptanceCriteria: App shell renders: top nav (h-12, slate-900 background, Space Grotesk branding), user avatar with display name, sign-out link; main content area (slate-50 background); minimum viewport 1280px

React Router v6 routes configured: /login (public), /search (PrivateRoute), /candidates/:id (PrivateRoute), /admin/* (AdminRoute); / redirects authenticated users to /search, unauthenticated to /login
FacetPanel renders five collapsible sections; each uses <fieldset> and <legend>; checkboxes for isSearchable: true taxonomy items sorted by sortOrder; candidateCount shown as muted badge

useSearchQuery hook parses URL params into typed SearchQueryParams and writes SearchQueryParams back to URL (bidirectional); filter values live in URL only — Zustand holds UI state only (panel open/closed)
Selecting a checkbox updates URL (?lang=python&framework=fastapi) without page reload; refreshing URL with params restores correct checkbox state
JetBrains Mono applied globally to all technical identifier elements; FacetPanel implemented at src/app/components/search/FacetPanel.tsx
userStories.notes: URL is the single source of truth for filter values — this is an MVP requirement, not a future enhancement. Zustand must only hold UI state (panel open/closed, hover). Back-navigation must preserve filter state via URL.

userStories.title: Firestore search query, results list, sort controls, and score badges
userStories.description: Implement the search query handler at src/handlers/search.ts: rarest-tag-first Firestore query + client-side AND filter + 200-doc cap + client-side sorting. Implement CandidateCard, SkillScoreBadge (indigo circle ● 87), AIMaturityBadge (violet pip bar ████░░ Lvl 3 or Not evaluated for null), StalenessTag, and ActiveFilterChips components. Add sort controls (Skill Score / AI Maturity / Last Scanned) persisted in URL. Wire useCandidates TanStack Query hook (staleTime 5min, loading skeleton).
acceptanceCriteria: src/handlers/search.ts builds Firestore query using rarest-tag-first (lowest candidateCount tag as primary array-contains filter), 200-doc cap, client-side AND for remaining tags

CandidateCard shows: GitHub username, avatar, SkillScoreBadge (indigo circle with score), AIMaturityBadge (violet pip bar with level or Not evaluated for null), top 3 matched skill tags, last_scanned date, StalenessTag if isStale: true
AIMaturityBadge renders null as dashed pip bar (░░░░░) + Not evaluated label; score 0 as empty circle pips + Level 0 — No AI signals label
ActiveFilterChips renders above results: one chip per active filter with × remove button; Clear all button removes all filter params from URL
Sort controls (dropdown/button group): Skill Score / AI Maturity / Last Scanned; selection updates URL ?sort=aiMaturityScore and re-executes query with correct orderBy
useCandidates TanStack Query hook: queryKey includes serialized params, staleTime 5min, enabled only when hasAnyFilter(params); loading skeleton shown while fetching
userStories.notes: The rarest-tag-first optimization is critical for query performance as pool grows. The SkillScoreBadge and AIMaturityBadge visual designs must match the spec exactly: indigo circle for skill, violet pip bar for AI maturity.

userStories.title: AI maturity min filter, thin-results state, and underserved query flagging
userStories.description: Implement the aiMaturityMin filter using two parallel Firestore queries merged client-side (scored >= N + unscored == null) to preserve null-inclusion. Implement ThinResultsState and ZeroResultsState components. Implement src/handlers/admin-flags.ts maybeFlagUnderservedQuery() that writes an underserved-query AdminFlag when results < 10, with 24-hour deduplication cooldown. Surface the suggested CLI command in the thin-results state.
acceptanceCriteria: When aiMaturityMin > 0 is selected, two parallel Firestore queries are executed: aiMaturityScore >= N (scored candidates at or above minimum) and aiMaturityScore == null (unscored, always included); results merged and sorted client-side
Unscored candidates (aiMaturityScore: null) always appear in results when aiMaturityMin filter is active — they are never excluded by the filter

ThinResultsState renders when results.length < 10 and > 0: result count, pool coverage limited message, exact scan discover CLI command with current filter params as --query, flagged confirmation message
ZeroResultsState renders when results.length === 0 with the same CLI command surface
maybeFlagUnderservedQuery() writes an admin_flags doc of type underserved-query with queryParams and resultCount when results < 10; does not re-flag same params within 24 hours
ThinResultsState and ZeroResultsState implemented in src/app/components/search/; Vitest test verifies deduplication cooldown logic
userStories.notes: Using a sentinel value (aiMaturityScore: -1) is explicitly prohibited — the two-query parallel merge preserves the null/0 invariant. The thin-results state must feel actively managed, not like a dead end.

userStories.title: Candidate profile page with full evidence sections
userStories.description: Build the candidate profile page at /candidates/:id. Load Candidate doc and linked Repository docs via TanStack Query. Render four EvidenceSection variants: skills (grouped language/framework/tool chips), repositories (repo list with GitHub links, language, star count, commit span, scanStatus), ai-signals (AI config files with modificationCount, isEvolved, diffComplexity, originSignal; coAuthoredByAI chip; aiAgentPatterns chips), evolution (timeline: file first seen → modifications → last modified → classification). Show SkillScoreBadge, AIMaturityBadge, StalenessTag, last_scanned, commitSpan.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a CandidateCard navigates to /candidates/:id; page loads Candidate doc by GitHub username; TanStack Query caches under ['candidate', id]; 404 state rendered if candidate not found
Page shows: GitHub username, avatar, GitHub profile link, SkillScoreBadge, AIMaturityBadge (null and 0 rendered distinctly), StalenessTag if isStale: true, last_scanned date, commitSpanMonths
EvidenceSection (skills) shows grouped chips: Languages, Frameworks, Tools — each chip is the taxonomy displayName

EvidenceSection (repositories) lists primaryRepoIds resolved to Repository docs: repo name, primary language, star count, commit span, scanStatus badge; each linked to GitHub URL (new tab); empty state if no repos

EvidenceSection (ai-signals) shows detected AI config files with modificationCount, isEvolved indicator, diffComplexity, originSignal; coAuthoredByAI chip; aiAgentPatterns chips; empty state if no signals

EvidenceSection (evolution) shows timeline-style display per config file: first seen → modification count → last modified → isEvolved classification; back navigation to search preserves URL filter state
userStories.notes: Repositories are loaded via a separate TanStack Query (not embedded in the main candidate query) to avoid loading all repos on every search result render. The profile must surface evidence, not assertions — every signal shown must trace back to actual repo data.

userStories.title: Admin UI — shell, pipeline trigger, job queue monitor, and flags tab
userStories.description: Build the protected /admin section with four-tab shell (Pipeline / Queue / Flags / Candidates). Pipeline tab: discovery run form (query, source, limit) with React Hook Form + Zod validation, queues discover job on submit with toast confirmation. Queue tab: jobs table with status filter tabs, 30-second auto-refresh via TanStack Query refetchInterval, retry and dismiss actions on failed jobs, AdminQueueRow component. Flags tab: underserved query list sorted by resultCount ASC with inline trigger-discovery action that queues discover job and sets flag actioned; repos-of-interest sub-section.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin shell renders four tabs (Pipeline / Queue / Flags / Candidates); deep-linking /admin?tab=queue opens Queue tab; non-admin redirected to /search

Pipeline tab form: Query (required), Source (select, default github), Limit (1-1000, default 100); submitting creates discover ScanJob with form values; toast confirms; form disabled during submission

Queue tab: jobs table columns (Type, Status, Created At, Attempts, Error truncated, Actions); status filter tabs (All/Pending/Running/Completed/Failed); auto-refreshes every 30s; failed job rows show errorMessage in tooltip/expandable row
Retry button on failed jobs: resets status to pending, attempts to 0, errorMessage to null; AdminQueueRow component at src/app/components/admin/AdminQueueRow.tsx

Flags tab: underserved queries listed by resultCount ASC; each row shows facet params, result count, flagged date, status badge; Trigger Discovery button opens inline form pre-filled with flagged query; submitting queues discover job and sets flag status to actioned
Repos-of-interest sub-section on Flags tab shows admin_flags of type repo-of-interest with detected signals and Mark as actioned button
userStories.notes: The Admin UI is an operational dashboard for a solo power user — information density is important. The Pipeline and Queue tabs provide the feedback loop Gabe needs to monitor and manage the scan pipeline day-to-day.

userStories.title: Admin candidates tab, rescan triggers, and inline AI Maturity Score assignment
userStories.description: Build the Candidates tab in the Admin UI. Show summary row (total candidates, count with AI Maturity Score assigned, count stale). Show taxonomy coverage breakdown (each language taxonomy item with candidateCount). Candidates table with columns: username, skillScore, aiMaturityScore (or Not evaluated), lastScanned, isStale. Rescan button per row creates rescan-candidate job. Expandable inline score assignment: segmented stepper [0][1][2][3][4][5] with auto-save calling updateAiMaturityScore() and TanStack Query cache invalidation.
acceptanceCriteria: Candidates tab summary row shows: total candidate count, count where aiMaturityScore is not null, count where isStale: true
Taxonomy coverage breakdown shows each language taxonomy item with its candidateCount
Candidates table columns: username, skillScore (SkillScoreBadge), aiMaturityScore (AIMaturityBadge or Not evaluated), lastScanned date, isStale indicator; stale rows visually highlighted
Rescan button per row creates a rescan-candidate ScanJob with priority: 1 (high priority) for that candidate's GitHub username

Expanding a row shows the inline score assignment: segmented stepper [0][1][2][3][4][5] with current score highlighted (or no highlight for null); clicking a level immediately calls updateAiMaturityScore(candidateId, score, adminUid) via src/handlers/candidates.ts

updateAiMaturityScore writes aiMaturityScore, aiMaturityScoredAt (serverTimestamp), aiMaturityScoredBy (admin UID) to Firestore; toast confirms; TanStack Query cache ['candidate', id] invalidated; row reflects new score immediately
userStories.notes: updateAiMaturityScore must only write the three aiMaturity fields — never touch skillScore or other pipeline-owned fields. The inline stepper is the primary ground-truth accumulation mechanism for the AI Maturity Model.

userStories.title: Theme switching, PAT expiry surface, E2E test suite, and Firebase Hosting deploy
userStories.description: Implement SettingsPopover with Light/Dark/Dim theme switching and font family selection (Space Grotesk/Inter/Outfit/IBM Plex Sans/Geist), persisted to localStorage, restored on load without flash. Implement PAT expiry/rate-limit error detection in the pipeline worker that writes an admin_flags system alert and surfaces a banner in the Admin UI Pipeline tab. Write the full Playwright E2E test suite covering all critical user journeys. Complete the Firebase Hosting deploy step in GitHub Actions CI gated on main branch.
acceptanceCriteria: SettingsPopover (gear icon in top nav) renders theme selector (Light/Dark/Dim) and font family selector; selecting theme applies Tailwind class to <html> and persists to localStorage; font applies via CSS variable; settings restored on load with no flash of wrong theme
JetBrains Mono remains as monospace for technical identifiers regardless of font family selection

Pipeline worker detects 401 (PAT expired) and writes an admin_flags document; Admin UI Pipeline tab shows a banner: GitHub API authentication error — PAT may have expired. Check your GITHUB_PAT env var; banner clears after next successful API call
